subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Social Proof in Scams
description: One-minute skill: Social Proof in Scams.

hook.text: Five-star reviews, celebrity endorsements, and packed seminars. All fake. All convincing.

buildup.text: Social proof means we trust things that others appear to trust. Scammers manufacture that proof.

discovery.text: Fake testimonials, paid crowds, and bot followers create the illusion of widespread trust.

twist.text: Even knowing about social proof doesn't make you immune. The instinct is deeply automatic.

climax.text: Every major scam in history used some form of manufactured social proof to recruit victims.

punchline.text: Popularity proves nothing except good marketing.

quiz.question: How do scammers use social proof?
options: By manufacturing fake testimonials, reviews, and crowds
